planting.note: Plant dormant crowns in early spring as soon as soil can be worked, setting the crown bud 1-2 inches below the soil surface.

directions: This classic English heirloom was selected specifically for its reluctance to bolt, so it channels far less energy into flower stalks than older rhubarb strains and instead keeps producing thick, tender leafstalks through most of the season. Divide and replant crowns every four to six years once the clump becomes congested, discarding the woody center and replanting vigorous outer sections. Top-dress heavily with compost or well-rotted manure each spring since rhubarb is a hungry, long-lived perennial, and remove any flower stalks promptly to redirect energy into stalk production. Stop harvesting by mid-summer to let the plant rebuild root reserves for the following year, and always discard the toxic leaf blades, using only the petioles.
